content:
The [Simple Interest Calculator](/simple-interest-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Interest on principal only — for short-term loans and deposits. Enter your principal, annual rate and time and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Simple interest is calculated only on the original principal, never on accumulated interest. It's used for many car loans, short-term notes and some savings products. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Finance tools include [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator), [Mortgage Calculator](/mortgage-calculator) and [Car Loan Calculator](/car-loan-calculator). People also look for this tool as "simple interest formula", "si calculator", "interest calculator".

## How to use the Simple Interest Calculator

Start by entering your principal, then entering your annual rate (%) and finally entering your time (years). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your principal.
2. Enter your annual rate (%).
3. Enter your time (years).
4. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
5. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

SI = P × R × T ÷ 100, and Total = P + SI.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Simple Interest Calculator](/simple-interest-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. 5,000 at 6% for 3 years earns 5,000 × 6 × 3 ÷ 100 = 900 interest, for a total of 5,900. Try the same figures in the [Simple Interest Calculator](/simple-interest-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Principal: 5000, Annual rate: 6 %, Time: 3 years), the [Simple Interest Calculator](/simple-interest-calculator) returns Simple interest: 900, Total amount: 5,900. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- For periods under a year, use months ÷ 12 as T.
- Compare with compound interest to see the difference over time.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### When is simple interest used?

Commonly for auto loans, short-term personal loans and certificates that pay interest out rather than reinvesting it. Try it with your own numbers in the [Simple Interest Calculator](/simple-interest-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is simple interest better for borrowers?

Yes — at the same rate, simple interest costs less than compound interest. Try it with your own numbers in the [Simple Interest Calculator](/simple-interest-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Simple Interest Calculator use?

SI = P × R × T ÷ 100, and Total = P + SI. You can see it in action in the [Simple Interest Calculator](/simple-interest-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Simple Interest Calculator?

Just Principal, Annual rate and Time. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
